title: Connected components of a finite-type scheme over a field are quasi-compact open finite-type subschemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $c\in C$, and let $T\subseteq |C|$ be its connected component, namely the maximal connected subset containing $c$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $T$ is open and quasi-compact (every cover of $T$ by open subsets has a finite subcover). With the open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], $T$ is a nonempty connected scheme of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof paragraph beginning 'Let $T$ be the connected component': the Noetherianity and open-component argument, without the smoothness assumption, with quasi-compactness and finite type of the open subscheme made explicit.

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $k$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$: a nonzero element of an ideal is invertible. Thus $k$ is Noetherian. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with coordinate ring $k$, makes $\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally Noetherian, and its one-point space is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the given structure map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Hence $C$ is a Noetherian scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], its closed subsets satisfy the minimal condition; equivalently its open subsets satisfy the ascending-chain condition.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Properties Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian, and Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open] to the underlying space of $C$, whose Noetherian hypothesis was verified in step 1. Its connected component $T$ containing $c$ is open. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] to the subset $T\subseteq |C|$: every open cover of $T$ has a finite subcover, so $T$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 04MF, lemma-locally-Noetherian-locally-connected; 04ME, lemma-locally-connected; 04ZA, lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact. This is the open-component inference in More on Morphisms Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type.

proof.text: Give $T$ the open subscheme structure $(T,\mathcal O_C|_T)$ and write $j:T\hookrightarrow C$ for its inclusion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its underlying topology is the subspace topology, so it is connected by the defining property of the connected component, and nonempty because it contains $c$. This is connectedness in [def-weil-connected-scheme].

For every affine open $V\subseteq C$, the inverse image $j^{-1}(V)$ is the subspace $T\cap V$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], applied to this subset of $|C|$. Its subspace topologies from $T$ and from $C$ coincide: a relatively open set in $T\cap V$ is the intersection with an open set of $C$. Thus every open cover in either topology has the same finite-subcover property. The affine-preimage definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] proves that $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism.

source.place: Tag 04ZA, lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact, part (2); Schemes Tag 01K4, lemma-quasi-compact-affine.

proof.text: The map $j$ is an open immersion and is quasi-compact by step 4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $j$ of finite type. Both $j$ and $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are now of finite type, so part (1) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes their composite $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of finite type. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves every clause.
